applicable_when: The kernel uses 255 registers/thread — the hardware maximum — because the 128×128 accumulator tile (16384 FP32 values) plus complex index arithmetic exhausts the register file. This limits the SM to only 2 active blocks (12.5% occupancy), leaving 58% of scheduler cycles with no eligible warp. The scheduler cannot hide memory latency. Simultaneously, BLOCK_K=32 with the current B-matrix load pattern causes severe shared memory bank conflicts (5.3-way average, 58% of wavefronts are excessive). Reducing BLOCK_M and BLOCK_N (e.g., to 64) halves the accumulator tile to 4096 values, dramatically cutting register usage and enabling 4–8× more active blocks per SM. Increasing BLOCK_K (e.g., to 64) improves arithmetic intensity per tile and reduces K-loop iterations. Adding @triton.autotune lets the runtime find the optimal configuration for this M=65536, N=2304, K=768 problem shape on H200.
